This record directly matches the role and meaning of x in the Blasius problem and supports the proposed exponent L=1 with all other exponents zero.

The problem variable y is the wall-normal coordinate measured normal to the plate. This entry applies directly to y in the original problem and supports the proposed exponent L=1 with all other exponents zero.

candidate_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: The streamwise velocity normalized by the free-stream speed is dimensionless. Dimensional analysis with the four provided variables yields a single independent similarity variable eta = y * sqrt(U/(nu x)), so u/U must be a function of this eta: u/U = F(eta). This is consistent with the Blasius boundary-layer similarity solution where u/U = f'(eta).

variables.reason: The problem variable U is the free-stream (external) flow speed. The KB entry pq_free_stream_velocity explicitly defines the velocity of the undisturbed flow outside a boundary layer and gives the SI dimension L T^-1 (dimension_vector [0,1,-1,0,0,0,0]), which supports the proposed exponents: L=1 and T=-1, with all other base exponents zero. pq_mean_flow_velocity and pq_velocity are general KB records for mean/bulk or generic velocity with the same SI dimension; they corroborate that U denotes a velocity in the fluid-mechanics/boundary-layer context and thus that the candidate vector applies to this variable in the original problem (free-stream speed U).

The problem variable nu is named as kinematic viscosity (momentum diffusivity). The KB record pq_kinematic_viscosity defines kinematic viscosity ν and gives SI dimension L^2 T^-1 (dimension_vector [0,2,-1,0,0,0,0]). That KB record directly applies to nu in this boundary-layer problem and fully supports the proposed exponents L=2 and T=-1, with other base exponents zero.

The problem variable x is the streamwise coordinate measured from the leading edge. The KB record pq_streamwise_distance defines streamwise distance (distance along the mean flow direction) and assigns SI dimension L (dimension_vector [0,1,0,0,0,0,0]). This record directly matches the role and meaning of x in the Blasius problem and supports the proposed exponent L=1 with all other exponents zero.

The problem variable y is the wall-normal coordinate measured normal to the plate. The KB entry pq_wall_normal_distance defines wall-normal distance and assigns SI dimension L (dimension_vector [0,1,0,0,0,0,0]). This entry applies directly to y in the original problem and supports the proposed exponent L=1 with all other exponents zero.

final_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: The streamwise velocity normalized by the free-stream speed is dimensionless. Dimensional analysis with the four provided variables yields a single independent similarity variable eta = y * sqrt(U/(nu x)), so u/U must be a function of this eta: u/U = F(eta). This is consistent with the Blasius boundary-layer similarity solution where u/U = f'(eta).
